references.text: The same instruction regarding the kidneys, the fat, and the lobe of the liver is given for the peace offering from cattle, showing the fixed procedure for sacrifices.
An identical description of which parts are to be removed from the sin offering, including the two kidneys with their fat and the lobe of the liver.
The guilt offering follows the same pattern with the removal of the kidneys, the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver.
At the consecration of Aaron and his sons, the fat, the lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys were burned on the altar—the same sacrificial parts as here.
During the priestly consecration, Moses took the fat, the lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys and burned them on the altar, in accordance with this instruction.
Aaron burned the fat, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver from the sin offering on the altar, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The fatty portions from the bull and the ram, including the fat tail, the internal fat, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver, were placed upon the breast pieces.
Shows the practical application of the specific requirements of the sacrificial law during the consecration of the priests.
Connects the sacrifice ritual to the historical ordination of priests through identical requirements for the parts of the sacrificial animal.
